_README: Copy to <engagement>.json and fill. Spec: ../ARTIFACTS.md. Working sample: ../examples/engagement.json
ANY change to targets, allowed_checks, or limits CHANGES THE FINGERPRINT and VOIDS the
existing authorization receipt. That is intended behaviour. Re-authorize.
This file is the TECHNICAL scope. It is NOT the authorization.
Legal sign-off, privacy sign-off, the system-owner signature, emergency contacts, SOC
deconfliction, rollback plans, and insurance notification live in the RoE:
Aegis SECURITY.md says the same thing: the receipt is a technical guardrail, not a
substitute for legal authorization, change control, stakeholder notification, or an
emergency plan. Do not let this JSON become a substitute for the signatures.
Remove the _README and _NOTES keys before use if your validator rejects unknown fields.
owner: <accountable system owner, a named human or team of record>

_NOTES.targets: ALLOW-LIST. No wildcards. Public addresses are DENIED unless the receipt explicitly opts in.
_NOTES.allowed_checks: Must exist in the fixed built-in registry. Run 'aegis-rt list-checks'. No plugins, no shell.
_NOTES.limits: These are BLAST-RADIUS CONTROLS, not performance tuning. Set them to the smallest values that let the engagement complete.
workflow: 2. aegis-rt plan <file>.json            -> capture the 64-char SCOPE FINGERPRINT
3. approval authority signs on THEIR machine (aegis-rt authorize ... --expires-at ...)
NEVER paste a fingerprint forward from an earlier plan -- that defeats the control
5. aegis-rt verify-ledger  ->  seal-ledger (by the approval authority)  ->  hand to White
